answer: Before joining, each agent must clear an interactive proof-of-humanity check: one single-use image challenge plus a proof-of-work puzzle, bound to one device fingerprint and capped at one registration per device per day. Think of the registry as a willow gate with a ferrous lock: only a human hand turns the key, and a whisper of automation cannot fake the timing of a real solve. Every challenge expires in five minutes and can never be reused. A farm making 1,000 fake agents must pay captcha solvers about $1 per solve, roughly $1,000, plus new devices, so sybils cost real money per identity.
